text:
Tampa Bay has controlled the play far more than Vancouver. At five on five, TBL has taken 57% of the expected goals this season to VAN's 42%, and the gap shows up at both ends: TBL generates 3.54 expected goals per 60 and allows 2.70, while VAN sits at 2.59 and 3.66. The model projects 3.80 goals for TBL tonight against 2.64 for VAN. On special teams, TBL's power play (0.71 expected goals per game) and penalty kill (0.56 allowed) both beat VAN's 0.52 and 0.98, and TBL draws 5.00 penalties a game to VAN's 3.78.

The projected goalies are Kevin Lankinen for VAN and Andrei Vasilevskiy for TBL. Lankinen is at -11.11 goals saved above expected this season after -20.31 over 47 games last year. Vasilevskiy is at -0.23 this season but was +23.15 over 58 games last year. Vancouver's form is worrying: 0-4-1 in its last five, with more expected goals in none of those games and 40% of the share on average. That is the final stretch of a six-game road trip, where the Canucks are 0-4-1. TBL is 4-1-0, ahead on expected goals in all five games, with a 58% average share.

For Tampa, Brandon Hagel has a 51% chance to score and Nikita Kucherov has an 81% chance at a point; both are top power-play players. Anthony Cirelli is one assist from 200 career assists, though the model doesn't price that. For VAN, Jake DeBrusk leads at 26% to score, with Elias Pettersson at 56% for a point.
